field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The rock fish and lingcod were on the bite up the coast this morning. There were a few halibut caught up the coast near 4 Mile beach. The anglers in Capitola caught some barracuda, halibut, and rock fish. The one boat who went to the Fingers found a nice temperature break and whales but did not see any tuna. The wind stayed down due to the fog and the swell was small. There are more boats looking for tuna in the next few days so we hope to get some report.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 10, 2026 Dime-Bright Kings Pour Into the Klamath Anglers Craig Vallely, left, and Steve Cowles with a nice Chinook salmon caught on the Lower Klamath river last Friday. Photo courtesy of Fishing the North Coast Guide Service Over the Labor Day holiday weekend, we were patiently waiting for the fall run of king salmon to begin their migration upriver. Well, the wait is over. Water temperatures cooled significantly thanks to dam releases and rain, and schools of ocean-fresh kings finally made their way into the lower river in big numbers beginning with Monday’s outgoing tide. This week, the fishing has been nothing short of spectacular from the Glen to well above Blue Creek. There are plenty of jacks to be had, and some really nice adults have shown up as well. The fish are dime-bright, with plenty still sporting seal lice, and they’re spread throughout the river. Most anglers have been able to quickly catch their limits and get off the water before the afternoon temperatures soar. As of last Thursday, 665 adults remained to be harvested from the 1,624-fish quota. With this week’s catch rate, the quota could be met after this weekend. Reminder: The spit

field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: The bottom fishing this morning was really good with lots of rockfish limits on the boats out this morning and there was a really nice number of Cabezon with also some nice Lingcod in the mix. Crabbing was up and down this morning depending on the boat. The Surfrider was out on a live bait and deep water Lingcod trip. Will repot on the results as soon as we get them.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: Darrel and Craig headed back to the honey hole and it started out a little slow but came on strong (bite has been late virtually every day this year). They plugged the boat with monsters. Pretty much everything right now is on bait, chasing birds and jumpers. This season was brutal but is a ton of fun right now. Better late than never. Mike C Great fishing. Plugged with pigs.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) in consultation with the State of Oregon, the Pacific Fishery Management Council, and fishery representatives met today via conference call and have taken the following in-season management action related to the ocean recreational non-mark-selective coho salmon season from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain: ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 12, 2026, at 11:59PM, the recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain is closed to the retention of coho salmon. The season remains open for all salmon except coho (Chinook salmon, 24” minimum length) with a daily bag limit of two salmon. RATIONALE: The Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain non-mark-selective (no fin-clip required) coho fishery opened on Tuesday September 1, 2026, with a quota of 25,700 coho salmon. As of Wednesday September 9, the coho salmon catch was estimated at 17,705 or approximately 69% of the total quota. Forecasting the coho harvest for the remainder of the season indicates that the quota will be exceeded by the scheduled end date of September 30. Fishery managers predict the fishery will reach 98% quota attainment at the end of the day on Saturday September 12
